section_summary: This section of decimal file 894.405 covers records from October 1947 to July 1948 concerning Japanese manners, customs, and social reform under the Allied Occupation. It includes War Department and State Department correspondence regarding a Japanese Ministry of Education directive that eliminated school-conducted ceremonial bowing toward the Imperial Palace and emperor-worship rituals. The section also contains Tokyo Despatch No. 428 transmitting Setsuko Hani's monograph, 'The Japanese Family System as Seen from the Standpoint of Japanese Women,' which critically examines the feudalistic patriarchal family system, the Meiji Civil Code, and the imperative for women's economic independence.

subfiles.about: A comprehensive monograph analyzing the feudal origins of Japan's family system, the legal subjugation of women under the Meiji Civil Code, and the requirement of economic independence for true female emancipation.
subfiles.summary: In this monograph published by the Japan Institute of Pacific Studies, Setsuko Hani critically examines the feudal foundations and patriarchal structure of the Japanese family ('ie') system. Drawing on judicial records, rural fieldwork, and personal case studies, she illustrates how property rights, primogeniture, and male headship have severely restricted women's legal capacity, marital freedom, and social status. While welcoming the equality provisions of the post-war Constitution, she argues that legal reform alone cannot emancipate women without concrete economic guarantees and broader social democratization.
subfiles.title: The Japanese Family System: As Seen from the Standpoint of Japanese Women
